scope: Browser functional acceptance on two preserved real device captures and current frontend fixtures. Xiaomi was identified and preflighted, but no new instrumented capture was produced because Magisk denies Shell root.

revision.head: f4cf92b8227fed470f11039e727338ca360f61ae
revision.tested_state: The existing uncommitted capture-budget implementation. This acceptance follow-up changes documentation and local evidence only; no product code was changed.

browser.transport: Authenticated loopback E2E adapter feeding the same QtraceService, SessionLoader, store and analysis used by the desktop. This is browser acceptance, not a native Tauri file-dialog or Android UI acceptance run.
browser.real_capture_method: Actual Chromium UI and Rust production service behind the existing authenticated E2E loopback transport; no response mocks or product-code changes.

fixture_suite.note: Existing fixture tests include intentional response interception for race, pagination and error scenarios. Real-capture checks below use no response mocks.

production_bundle.proof: Production selects the Tauri bridge, reports its unavailability in a plain browser, and makes no fetch requests to the E2E loopback adapter.

real_capture_results.name: flight
real_capture_results.fixture_mapping: Byte-identical copy under a private fixture_root/sessions/valid-mixed, selected by the existing E2E dialog adapter. Source reports and artifacts are unchanged; report paths and hashes are still validated by the production SessionLoader.

new_instrumented_capture.required_external_action: In Magisk on Xiaomi, allow superuser access for Shell (com.android.shell, UID 2000). After it is allowed, rerun the root probe, start the matching frida-server and execute new qtrace captures.

limitations: Browser success applies to the explicitly identified historical report hashes. It is not a new Xiaomi capture or proof of a new Xiaomi capture-to-browser run.

The real-capture browser run checks selected pages, distant scrolling, representative register/call-tree/memory queries and persistence. The separate capture-budget record contains complete offline event and pagination checks.
These are functional checks. Browser latency, layout, accessibility, fixed-host performance, native Tauri integration and a complete device release gate were not comprehensively certified.
The original incomplete Flight capture still contains its recorded gaps and termination uncertainty.
Raw traces/screenshots are local ignored artifacts. Ephemeral E2E services were stopped after the checks.
